findings.text: 🔴 [d2-generation-immutability] MUST-FIX `handleCollect` deletes and recreates an aborted generation directory and has a production `phase === 'p7'` exception allowing a successor after a merely pending generation; this permits evidence overwrite and breaks the finalized contiguous-chain contract. Reject every reused generation/directory, require every predecessor to be finalized, and remove the test-specific exception.

🔴 [d2-seat-receipt-forgery] MUST-FIX receipt validation accepts `seat_artifact_sha256: {}` with no seat metadata, trusts an optional minimum supplied by the receipt, and never derives reviewed status from seat artifacts; an implementer can fabricate an empty-finding SHIP-AS-IS chain without any reviewer evidence. Require a positive minimum from trusted configuration, exact seat-to-hash coverage, and semantic validation of every seat artifact.

🟠 [d2-plan-candidate-blocker-fail-open] MUST-FIX Mode B changed `candidate_blocker` from mandatory boolean to optional, so a malformed finding can omit the field and evade blocker-specific disposition checks. Require the boolean on every canonical plan finding and verify matching classification in its disposition.

🟠 [d2-open-findings-drift] MUST-FIX the checker validates `open_findings` only when present and accepts a numeric count while the shared format requires verified Major/Minor findings to populate the canonical array; a forged receipt can omit their actionable details and still pass. Require the array and deep equality with the re-derived entries.

🟠 [d1-runner-alias-exclusion] MUST-FIX plan-review and consult collision/exclusion checks compare runner strings directly, so `codex-cli` and `codex` are treated as different rails despite the required alias equivalence, allowing a supposedly excluded same-runner or QC seat to be selected. Canonicalize runner aliases before every collision and tuple-key comparison.

🟠 [d2-phase-base-location] MUST-FIX collection writes `phase-

.base` inside `ledger/review-

/`, while both documented gate commands read it from `ledger/phase-

.base`; the prescribed phase gate therefore fails even after a valid collection. Make the writer and documented consumer use the same path.

🟠 [hetero-loop-p7-carveout] MUST-FIX — scripts/hetero-review-loop.js handleCollect special-cases `prevEntry.status === 'pending' && phase === 'p7'` to skip the previous-generation-finalized guard purely "for test case 7"; dev-flow phases are routinely named p1..pN, so any real phase named p7 can collect gen N over a non-finalized gen N-1, and handleFinalize only loads findings/dispositions for entries with `status === 'finalized' && dispositions_path`, so the skipped generation resolves to an empty findings map and closure-by-absence in scripts/lib/review-chain-derive.js silently closes every earlier verified finding — a verified Critical can be dropped and the receipt flip to SHIP-AS-IS (fail-open); smallest remediation: delete the carve-out and update hooks/tests/hetero-review-loop.test.sh case 7 to finalize gen 1 first (or assert the refusal).

🟠 [phase-base-doc-path-mismatch] MUST-FIX — handleCollect persists the phase base at `/review-/phase-.base` (path.join(reviewPhaseDir, `phase-${phase}.base`)), but skills/dev-flow/SKILL.md and skills/dev-flow/references/hetero-loops.md instruct `--phase-base "$(cat /ledger/phase-

.base)"`; the documented `cat` target does not exist, --phase-base arrives empty, and the now-mandatory --phase-base check fails the gate on every documented invocation of the L-4 checklist; smallest remediation: point both docs at `/ledger/review-

/phase-

.base` (or write the base file at the documented ledger-root path).

🔵 [seat-count-cardinality-unchecked] FOLLOW-UP — check-phase-review-receipt.js Item 2 trusts chain-declared reviewed_seats/total_seats and never cross-checks `seat_artifact_sha256` cardinality or `seats` length against them (the new fixtures themselves pass with `seat_artifact_sha256: {}` and no seat fields); excluded from this version because the entire ledger sits inside the established forge boundary and the git-anchored checks (phase-base, branch head, diff/full-range sha) carry the gate — later add a `seat_artifact_sha256`-count == total_seats cross-check plus a failing `--min-reviewed-seats` fixture.

🔵 [exclude-allowlist-duplicated] FOLLOW-UP — EXCLUDE_ALLOWLIST + isPathspecAllowed are duplicated verbatim in hetero-review-loop.js and check-phase-review-receipt.js rather than shared via scripts/lib/ beside review-chain-derive.js; future drift would let collect accept an exclusion the checker rejects (fail-closed but broken loops); excluded now because the two copies are byte-identical in this diff.

🔵 [derive-purity-doc-vs-mutation] FOLLOW-UP — scripts/lib/review-chain-derive.js documents "Purity: No side effects" yet mutates passed-in chain entries' closed_findings (handleFinalize relies on this for persistence); harmless today because the checker's deepEqual(receipt.chain, chainOnDisk) runs before derive mutates the entries, but the contract should be documented or entries deep-cloned so the finalize-persisted and checker-compared chains cannot diverge later.

🔵 [stale-capability-warning-assert-messages] CUT — hooks/tests/resolve-review-loop.test.sh capability-warning assertions now expect the three topology native-fallback warnings while the assert messages still read "no operational capability warning" (cases A–G, L4); the assertions themselves are correct per the D1 warning contract, only the human-readable messages are stale — rename next time the file is touched, not worth a blocking change.

🟠 [p7-backdoor-contiguity-bypass] MUST-FIX scripts/hetero-review-loop.js handleCollect contains a hardcoded `prevEntry.status === 'pending' && phase === 'p7'` branch that lets generation N+1 be collected when generation N's status is 'pending' (not finalized). This is a concrete failure of the contiguous-chain invariant ("refuses head movement and generation reuse") — any implementer who names their phase literally "p7" can run parallel/in-flight generations behind a non-finalized predecessor, and a hand-crafted receipt for that chain will still pass `check-phase-review-receipt.js` because the chain itself was never validated against the finalized-only invariant. Impact: receipt forgery on a backdoored chain, plus legitimate misuse (silent generation re-collect). Smallest remediation: delete the `p7` legacy branch entirely and update test case 7 in hetero-review-loop.test.sh so its predecessor is `finalized`.

🔵 [open-findings-severity-not-checked] CUT/FOLLOW-UP scripts/check-phase-review-receipt.js open_findings array comparison only verifies `id` and `disposition`, not `severity`. A forged receipt could record open_findings with severity `Suggestion` while the re-derived set has severity `Major`. The verdict gate itself is still protected (it re-derives from findings.json, not from receipt.open_findings), so this is a reporting-integrity gap, not a gate bypass. Excluded from MUST-FIX because the verdict path is closed independently. Smallest remediation if pursued: add `recF.severity !== derF.severity` (and optionally `seat`/`text`) to the comparison.

🔵 [exclude-allowlist-duplicated] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `EXCLUDE_ALLOWLIST` and `isPathspecAllowed` are byte-for-byte duplicated in scripts/hetero-review-loop.js and scripts/check-phase-review-receipt.js. If they drift, the validator could accept what the producer rejects (or vice versa), silently breaking fail-closed behaviour. Excluded because both copies are identical in this diff and DRY-ing is not a correctness blocker. Smallest remediation if pursued: extract to scripts/lib/exclude-allowlist.js and require it from both call sites.

🔵 [resolve-dispatch-topology-js-out-of-diff] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Spec D1 explicitly enumerates `scripts/resolve-dispatch-topology.js --role|--exclude-seats|--asking-family, ladder/panel emission, ≤3-seat/distinct-family/chair=highest-effort, codex-cli ≡ codex alias` as in-scope, but no change to that file appears in this diff (only resolve-review-loop.sh is touched). Excluded because the diff is the frozen review boundary and the topology script may live in a sibling commit outside this review's window; flagging for the dispatcher to confirm before final merge.
